scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.

F-01.statement: Across 2440 dispute tickets, median response time is 1.6 days and p90 is 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA.

F-02.statement: Dispute ticket volume was ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) and rose to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (1180, 1260), confirming the surge began in August and roughly doubled.

F-03.statement: Of disputed bills, 1240 are tagged ESTIMATED read type and 1785 are tagged ACTUAL read type.

F-04.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records, indicating no tariff changes are recorded in that log.

F-05.statement: Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a target of 0.95, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request field route priority changes but requires execution only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation.

F-07.statement: 320 distinct accounts were billed on estimated reads last cycle, across 40 distinct routes.

F-08.statement: Among disputed bills with ESTIMATED read type, 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff but rejected during billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (exported_to_billing=true), while 56 had no AMI read received before cutoff (NO_READ_RECEIVED, exported_to_billing=false).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem; automating ticket responses (and bill fixes) would resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused systematically incorrect bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI read events from the MDMS vendor failed to deliver or validate (H-MDMS-BILL), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter-read uploads from the field contractor (H-FIELD-BILL) became incomplete or invalid, increasing estimate substitution and billing errors.

H-ROUTE-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: Field route completion dropped due to staffing shortfalls, leaving more meters unread and billed on estimates (SH-FIELD's framing).

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data shows dispute ticket response handling is currently performing within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA, n=2440), which undercuts the requester's (SH-CS) framing that slow/inadequate ticket response is driving the surge; the surge is more likely explained by an upstream billing-accuracy cause rather than response speed.

CRM data (E-02) shows monthly dispute volume of ~600 (Jun 610, Jul 590) then jumping to ~1180-1260 (Aug 1180, Sep 1260), confirming the surge's timing (onset in August) and roughly doubling magnitude as described in the initial request. This is a confirmation of the symptom's scale and timing, not evidence of its cause.

Of disputed bills, 1785 (59%) were on ACTUAL (not estimated) reads versus 1240 (41%) on ESTIMATED reads, so the majority of disputes involve bills where a real meter read was obtained, not estimate substitution.

The tariff change log in billing-db contains zero records, meaning no tariff changes are logged there — this rules out a tariff-rate change as the cause of the billing dispute surge, but does not speak to read-type substitution, rule changes, or handoff failures already under investigation.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; as a stakeholder statement it is non-authoritative but it agrees in direction with the already-established authoritative E-04 finding (zero tariff-change log records), reinforcing that tariff change is not the surge cause without adding new independent evidence.

Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, across 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. roughly 12% of scheduled manual-read routes were not completed — a quantified shortfall rather than confirmation of its downstream effect on billing or its root cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative) attributes late/incomplete manual-read routes to a reader staffing shortfall since July, offering a causal explanation for why some customers receive estimated bills, consistent with their stated incentive to justify headcount increase.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is a service-contract clause establishing that route priority changes may be requested by the utility but must be executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), which is the documentary basis for the already-active K-DISPATCH authority constraint rather than new information about the billing dispute root cause.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation records 320 distinct accounts billed on estimated reads last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes — a small subset relative to the 9200 manual-read accounts in E-06, indicating estimate substitution currently affects a limited account population rather than being widespread.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor-side, non-authoritative) reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471), suggesting the ACCESS_PENDING hold on mdms-export may be clearable; this is a stakeholder claim, not a verified tool-health or data change, so it does not yet confirm actual data availability or semantic validity.

For disputed bills tagged ESTIMATED read type, AMI telemetry (E-11) shows 1184 cases had an AMI read received before cutoff that billing import rejected with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (still exported to billing), versus only 56 cases with true non-delivery (NO_READ_RECEIVED). This identifies a billing-import validation behavior that discards high-consumption AMI reads and falls back to estimate substitution as the dominant driver of the ESTIMATED-dispute subset, rather than field route or MDMS-delivery failure.

U-ACCURACY-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether dispute-volume recovery alone is sufficient to validate success, or whether the billing-error-rate audit must also pass before declaring the problem resolved.
U-ACCURACY-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Cross-check a sample of non-disputed bills in billing-db for the same error pattern to confirm dispute volume captures the true error population.
U-ACCURACY-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Use dispute volume as an interim indicator while separately tracking the billing-error-rate metric before declaring recovery.

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200+/month (Aug-Sep) (E-02), driven by a defect introduced around August in the billing import + validation step of meter-to-cash, which produces incorrect bills predominantly for accounts with ACTUAL (not estimated) meter reads (E-03: 59% actual vs 41% estimated among disputed bills). This is not explained by slow ticket handling, which remains within SLA (E-01), nor by a tariff change, which the log shows did not occur (E-04/E-05), nor primarily by estimate substitution from field/AMI read failures, since actual-read bills dominate the dispute population (E-03).

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and automatically fix whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01), after dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1200+/month between July and August-September (E-02). Investigation established the real problem differently from that framing: ticket response times remain within SLA (E-01), ruling out slow handling as the cause, and no tariff change occurred (E-04, E-05), ruling that out too. Instead, 59% of disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not estimated) meter reads (E-03), and the only confirmed mechanism (E-11) is a billing-import rule that rejects certain AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and falls back to estimates - which explains the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputes but not why ACTUAL-read bills, the majority, are wrong. The system released two read-only capabilities - analyze_disputed_bills (DA-BILL) and monitor_dispute_volume (DA-TICKET) - under a RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION decision with no holds, because no automated bill writes or rule changes are permitted (K-BILLWRITE) and the deeper diagnostic/remediation work could not be completed in available time and tool access.
key_points: Requester's framing (CL-01: slow ticket response) was tested and rejected: E-01 shows median 1.6d / p90 2.8d response, within the 3.0-day SLA, despite the ~doubling of volume (E-02).
A tariff change was ruled out as a cause: billing-db's tariff_change_log has zero records (E-04), consistent with SH-BILL's statement (E-05, non-authoritative).

Dispute volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-02), and 59% of disputed bills are on ACTUAL reads vs 41% on ESTIMATED (E-03), meaning most disputes are not simple estimate substitution.

H-RULE-CHANGE (a billing-import validation defect around August) is the SUPPORTED hypothesis, backed by E-03, E-09, E-11; H-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE was REJECTED and H-SLOW-RESPONSE-FRAMING was REJECTED (contradicted by E-01).

The confirmed mechanism (E-11: 1184 AMI reads rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION vs 56 true non-delivery) explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset via AMI rejection/estimate fallback, but does not explain why ACTUAL-read bills (the 59% majority) are incorrect - this scope mismatch was flagged by verification (seq 200) and is the named limitation driving the release decision.

Released scope is limited to two read-only analysis/monitoring deliverables (analyze_disputed_bills:DA-BILL, monitor_dispute_volume:DA-TICKET); diagnose_billing_rule_change and analyze_ami_read_events were part of the intended scope but not completed.

Field-staffing (H-ROUTE-STAFFING-SHORTFALL, from SH-FIELD's claim E-07/CL-03) and field-handoff-failure (H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE) hypotheses remain CANDIDATE status but are contradicted by E-03, E-09, E-11.

No bill corrections or billing-config rule changes were or could be executed by this system: write_bill_adjustment requires SH-BILL authority (K-BILLWRITE) and there is no write capability for billing-config in the tool surface.
limitations_explained: Semantic gap (root_cause_mechanism_scope_mismatch, flagged at verify seq 200): the confirmed defect mechanism (E-11) accounts for the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset only, not for why ACTUAL-read bills - the majority per E-03 - are also disputed; root cause for the dominant dispute population remains unconfirmed.
